study.title: Matthew 6: Life before God, without ostentation, without anxiety
study.overview: Matthew 6 gathers Jesus" teachings on true piety, inner devotion, and practical trust in the Father. The chapter contrasts the religion made to be seen with the life lived before God in secret; then it teaches the disciple's prayer, the need for forgiveness, fasting without theatricality, the correct use of goods and freedom before anxiety. The thread is simple: the Father sees, knows, provides and should be sought above all else.

outline.title: Esmola in secret
outline.explanation: Jesus warns against acts of justice done to receive applause. Smamola must be born of sincerity, not of vanity, because human reward replaces the reward of the Father when the intention is to be seen.

outline.title: Prayer and fasting with sincerity
outline.explanation: Prayer should not imitate the display of the hypocrites or the empty repetition of the Gentiles. Jesus teaches our Father as a model of dependence, reverence and submission, and applies the same principle to fasting: practice must be discreet, turned to God, and not to public recognition.

outline.title: Treasury, Vision and Dealer
outline.explanation: The disciple must accumulate treasures in heaven, because the heart follows what values most. The eye symbolizes inner guidance: if it is pure, the person will be full of light; if it is bad, life will be dominated by darkness. Therefore no one can serve God and riches at the same time.

outline.title: Trust in the Father and Kingdom Priority
outline.explanation: Jesus forbids anxiety about food, drink, clothing and tomorrow, not because the needs are unreal, but because the Father knows and sustains his children. Birds and lilies serve as examples of divine providence. The disciple must first seek the Kingdom of God and his righteousness, trusting that the necessary will be added.

study.context: The chapter presupposes known religious practices in the Jewish environment, such as alms, prayer and fasting, and also confronts ways of piety linked to appearance. The notes provided indicate that the Lord's prayer is similar to a common Jewish prayer, but Jesus gives it as a brief and orderly expression of the new faith of his followers. The teaching scenario is pastoral: Jesus corrects religious deviations that value reputation, wealth and immediate security.
study.theology: Matthew 6 teaches that true righteousness is relational and before God, not performable before people. The heavenly Father is presented as the one who sees in secret, knows needs before the request, forgives, sustains and governs. The prayer of the disciple unites reverence to the name of God, desire for the Kingdom, submission to the divine will, daily dependence, confession of sin, practice of forgiveness and request for deliverance. Trust in God does not eliminate responsibility, but redefines priorities: the Kingdom comes first, and the necessary goods are under the providence of the Father. Anxiety is treated as incompatible with mature faith, because it reveals difficulty in resting in divine care.

scholarViews.insight: The chapter presents justice as a service to God and not as a search for human recognition; godly life includes almsgiving, prayer and fasting, practiced with discretion to counter the tendency to seek applause.
Prayer is treated as proof of spiritual sincerity: the true disciple now, and the instruction of Jesus corrects hypocrisy and guides devotion to God, not to men.
The final petition on tomorrow teaches that anxious concern is useless and invasive, for the future belongs to God; the believer should not anticipate with fear what has not yet happened.

questions: Have my spiritual practices been made to please God or to strengthen my image before people?
What, in practice, has occupied the place of treasure in my heart: the Kingdom of God or material security?
In which areas do I need to exchange anxiety for concrete trust in the Father's daily care?
study.practice: Choose a practice of devotion this week, such as offering, prayer or fasting, and do so without announcing anyone, with an explicit intention to honor God. In addition, identify a recurring concern and turn it into simple prayer, giving God the today rather than trying to control tomorrow. He also practice forgiveness concretely with someone who has offended him, remembering that the text links forgiveness received and forgiveness granted.
study.uncertainty: The notes provided limit historical contextualization; therefore, it is not possible to state details about customs, locations or dates beyond what the text itself and the excerpts allow. In particular, reading on the use of trumpet in alms is presented as likely in the notes, not as absolute data of the chapter. References to Jewish parallels in our Father and ancient linguistic uses should be treated as an interpretation of the commentators, not as an undeniable conclusion of the biblical text.
